title: Zion’s record should list only those who keep consecration
setting: Joseph Smith returned to Kirtland, Ohio, on 6 November 1832 after a trip east with Newel K. Whitney. On 27 November he wrote a letter to William W. Phelps in Independence, Missouri. Phelps had reported in print that 810 Saints had moved to Zion and asked whether all had kept the law. Some had arrived without consecrating property and so had no inheritance from the bishop. This section is an extract of that letter, printed in January 1833 and added to the Doctrine and Covenants in 1876.
summary: The letter says the Lord’s clerk must keep a history and record of all that happens in Zion. The record lists those who consecrate property and receive inheritances, with their faith and works. Those who do not receive inheritances by consecration are not to be enrolled with God’s people. Their genealogy is not to be kept in the Church’s records. Joseph Smith then quotes what he calls the still small voice. It says God will send one “mighty and strong” to set the house in order and divide inheritances by lot. The man who steadies the ark will fall, and those not written in the book will have no inheritance among the Saints.

contextNote.title: Why a list of names mattered
contextNote.text: Phelps faced a practical question: who counted as a settled member of Zion? Verse 1 assigns the clerk to record those who consecrate and receive inheritances. Verse 3 says those who did not consecrate should not be enrolled with God’s people. Verse 4 extends this to their genealogy in Church records. Verse 12 points to Ezra 2:61–62, where priests without a record lost their office. In this passage, being written down is a record of covenant kept, not just a count of settlers.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 85–87, “Stand Ye in Holy Places,” includes this letter about keeping records in Zion. Besides names, what does verse 2 say the clerk should record, and why might that matter?

jsp.title: Letter to William W. Phelps, 27 November 1832

reviewNote: Read all 12 verses. Heading gives Kirtland, 27 November 1832, an extract from a letter to Phelps in Independence about Saints who had not consecrated. JSP historical introduction gives the 6 November return, Phelps’s report of 810 emigrants, John Whitmer as the clerk, the January 1833 extract, and 1876 inclusion. The text does not name the clerk; John Whitmer is listed from JSP. The identity of the “one mighty and strong” and the man who steadies the ark is not discussed, since neither source settles it. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes.
